steps.name: Iteration 1: graph-based planning
steps.prompt:
Work only in C:/GIT/Argus/experiments/knowledge-loop. Build Workshop Studio: a polished local web app for workshop discovery, bookings and waitlists. This is a development-process experiment: durable business knowledge and traceable decisions matter as much as the UI. Use synthetic data; no payment services or deployment. Follow SOLID and keep the scope small. Do not commit, push, or alter Argus source or other projects. Stage only this app's changes when handing off. Every invocation is fresh: read the project's brief, relevant iteration documents and ARGUS_KNOWLEDGE_CONTEXT_FILE before acting. Never edit Argus's canonical knowledge store or read another project's claims. Publish knowledge only through ARGUS_KNOWLEDGE_DELTA_FILE using the injected contract. Keep assumptions explicit, never describe an assumption as verified. Reference consumed and premise claims by the exact supplied ID:vN. New claims use localId, never invented canonical IDs. Never edit Argus's supplied context files. Stop and report blocked on a missing prerequisite or conflicting requirements; never invent success or retry a failed fix without fresh diagnosis. No background work may remain at completion.

Read all supplied canonical knowledge, including earlier decisions and learning, plus docs/business-brief.md and existing verification reports. Write docs/iterations/1/decision.md and docs/iterations/1/decision.json. Compare at least three feasible next increments by user value, evidence strength, dependency readiness and risk. Choose exactly one small increment; for iteration 1 it must produce a runnable end-to-end MVP. Later choices must respond to previous verification or business findings, not simply follow a predefined feature list. Cite exact premise refs and show why the alternatives lost. Record acceptance criteria, preserved rules, test plan, uncertainties and intended changes. Write a KnowledgeDelta containing at most two claims: a decision justified by supplied premises, and optionally an explicitly labelled assumption. Record consumed refs and attach evidence to the decision document. Preserve previous decisions as history; a new choice must not silently rewrite them. The final message must include the selected option, alternatives and premise refs.

name: H2 Shadow Evidence — 5 runs per hour

steps.name: Evaluate one case honestly
steps.prompt: This is a controlled, read-only business scenario benchmark for Argus H2 shadow measurement. Use the Bash tool to run exactly `node select-case.mjs` in the current directory, without a cd prefix or other commands. This exact command is pre-authorized. The selector reads ARGUS_RUN_ID from the actual process environment; do not infer environment availability from the prompt. If the command is denied, report the permission denial rather than claiming an environment variable is absent. Do not use PowerShell or inspect any additional file. Read the selected scenario, then fulfil its task using only the supplied facts. Return the corpus tag, scenario ID, run ID, calculation or reasoning, and the requested decision. Check your arithmetic and constraints. If a requested exact answer cannot be derived because required information is missing or the constraints contradict each other, explain exactly why and honestly report blocked against that task; do not invent data or silently choose which rule to ignore. A feasible task with a negative business decision is still successfully answered. Do not write any file, access the network, inspect other projects, or change Argus stores. Do not invoke skills, delegate, start background work, or perform implementation. Finish with a concise plain-text result, with enough evidence for a later reviewer to understand whether the task was accomplished. This controlled workload measures collection and trace sensitivity; it does not establish production failure rates or cause-label accuracy.
